A 202 foot memorial located on the aptly named Monument Street commemorates this event, which followed a similar event 32 years earlier and whose aftermath saw the execution of Robert Hubert. Thomas Bloodworth exhausted the effects of this event with his indecisiveness, which had its roots at a business owned by Thomas Farynor. On the second day, the future King James II joined in the efforts to suppress this event, which notably destroyed St. Paul's Cathedral. Documented in the memoirs of Samuel Pepys was, what 1666 disaster which resulted in the destruction of much of the capital of England?

Contested in Hardin County, this battle took its more common name from a church around which many of the Union soldiers were flanked. Beginning with William Hardee's surprise attack, this engagement's first day saw Lew Wallace send his division in the wrong direction, as well as the death of Albert Sydney Johnston. Union lines at the Hornet's Nest prevented an attack under P.G.T. Beauregard until the second day, which ended in a Confederate retreat to Corinth. The shores of the Tennessee River were the site of U.S. Grant's victory at, what April 1862 battle known in the north as Pittsburg Landing.

This man served as a provincial governor during the rule of his older brother Mongke, whose death resulted in a three year civil war between this man and his younger brother Ariq Boke. During his reign, this ruler moved his capital to Dadu and this son of Tolui also attempted to conquer Japan twice, but his fleet was destroyed both times by a divine wind, or kamikaze. He had a home suitable for a son of God built in Xanadu, described as a stately pleasure-dome by Samuel Taylor Coleridge. Marco Polo famously visited, what 13th century ruler, founder of Yuan dynasty, the grandson of a more famous Mongol emperor.

William Henry Harrison appointed Lancaster, Ohio native Thomas Ewing Jr. To this position, which was held by Roger B. Taney prior to becoming Supreme Court Chief Justice. The most famous man to hold this position was succeeded by Oliver Wolcott Jr., and it has been held by men such as Albert Gallatin, Levi Woodbury, and Andrew Mellon. The first man to hold it wrote the majority of the Federalist Papers and died following a duel with Aaron Burr. Identify this Cabinet position first held by Alexander Hamilton.

He served as a Major of Artillery during the Siege of Toulon and was promoted to brigadier-general afterwards. Later, he conquered the Papal States after the Battle of the Bridge of Arcole. His Egyptian expedition saw a decisive victory for him at the Battle of Embabeh but a disastrous defeat at the hands of Horatio Nelson at the Battle of the Nile. The Battle of Borodino forced back the Grande Armee of - for 10 points - what French emperor whose Hundred Days came to an end with a final exile to Saint Helena after his last defeat at Waterloo?

This man was originally only supposed to act as regent for his infant nephew, Amyntas IV. Held as a hostage in his youth by Thebes, he received his military and diplomatic education from Epaminondas of Thebes. While in power, this man intervened in the Social War to gain land and resources for his kingdom, fought the Third Sacred War, and made threats on Sparta. However his reign over Greece ended in 336 BC when he was assassinated by one of his bodyguards. Name this King of Macedonia, father of Alexander.

This man rose to the rank of major when he retired from the army at age 22 in 1865. His election to Congress in 1876 was in part helped by Rutherford B. Hayes, and he chaired the Committee on Ways and Means from 1889 to 1891. His namesake tariff act set an average rate for imports at 48.4% and he used his advocacy of the gold standard and a brilliant advertising campaign designed by Mark Hanna to become the last Civil War veteran elected President in 1896. What president, defeated William Jennings Bryant before being assassinated by Leon Czolgosz in 1901?

The Torstenson War was a continuation of this conflict as Sweden launched a surprise attack on Denmark-Norway, winning control of the Baltic Sea as a result. One of the sides was thoroughly weakened when the Danish had to pull out of the war while being attacked by the troops of Albrecht von Wallenstein. A major turning point happened when, at the first battle of Breitenfeld, the Catholic troops were defeated and Germany was opened up to Protestant forces by the forces of Gustavus Adolphus. Name this war which began with the Defenestration of Prague, and ended with the Treaty of Munster, part of the Peace of Westphalia.

This politician was appointed Minister to France in 1794 and was able to secure the release of Thomas Paine. With Pinckney, this politician attempted to negotiate a treaty with Britain over impressments as a renewal of the Jay Treaty. He sent Andrew Jackson to terminate the conflict in Florida in 1817 and saw the US gain that territory by terms of the Adams-Onis Treaty, negotiated by his Secretary of State, John Quincy Adams. Overseeing the Era of Good Feelings, identify this US President who has a namesake doctrine that forbid further colonization in the Western Hemisphere.

This man was taken out of action due to severe wounds while trying to scale a fort at the Battle of Horseshoe Bend during the War of 1812. Raised by the Cherokees in his teenage years, he often fought for the rights of Native Americans, which led to the beating of Congressman William Stanbery. He was then forced to leave the country, moving to the then-Mexican territory of Texas, where he led Texan troops to victory at the Battle of San Jacinto, giving Texas its independence. Name this first president of the Republic of Texas, the namesake of its most populous city.
